Teddy is a Pembroke Welsh Corgi
who knows a ton of tricks. His
person, Doc Leo, is a friendly
hobo clown, and tonight he is
the star of the Clown Club's
Big Show. But Teddy's big
sister Gwinn just ran off with
Doc Leo's costume suitcase and
scattered it all over town.
No nose, no show!

Hop, bark, dig, high five, sit
pretty, spin, play dead and
roll over your way across
town. Find every piece of the
costume and get it to the show
on time!

  the PC speaker works too.

  3        spin
  4        play dead (hold)

  F1 help     F2 status
  F3 music    F4 sound

pages.head: The Story
pages.html:
TEDDY'S LITTLE BIG ADVENTURE

A little dog. A big town. A ton of tricks.

Teddy is a Pembroke Welsh Corgi. He is short. He is fluffy. He has the most famous rump on the block, and he knows a ton of tricks.

His person is Doc Leo, a friendly hobo clown with a chewed-up felt fedora, wire glasses, a painted-on ash beard, a green tie and red sneakers. He walks a rubber chicken on a dog leash. Doc Leo is a proud member of the Clown Club: he twists balloon animals, does magic tricks - there is always a dove in that hat - and marches in every parade in town. Tonight is the Clown Club's Big Show. Guess who the star is.

Teddy also has a big sister. Gwinn is a chocolate-brown pit-lab mix, younger than Teddy but twice his size. She was adopted, and she is still learning: she has never once sat when asked. She knows one trick, and it is zoomies. This morning Doc Leo drove ahead to the Clown Club in his little red CitiCar and left his costume suitcase on the back step. Gwinn found it, ran off with it, and galloped all over town. The fedora, the green tie, the red sneakers, the rubber chicken and the red nose went flying, and his balloon dogs floated away.

No nose, no show! Doc Leo is already at the Clown Club. Only a little dog can save the Big Show.

pages.head: Getting Started
pages.html:
Getting Started

Type TEDDY and press Enter. You need a VGA display. A Sound Blaster (or compatible) plays the music and the digitized woofs, yips and honks; without one, the PC speaker beeps along gamely.

A cartoon plays first: watch Gwinn make off with the suitcase (pick Read Storyline to see it again). Press any key to get to the menu, then pick Play. Leave the menu alone for half a minute and Teddy will show you around the backyard himself.

There are five stops on Teddy's adventure. Before each one, a card shows which stop it is (LEVEL 2 OF 5), where you are, which piece of Doc Leo's costume to look for, and which trick is new. At the end of every stop, Doc Leo's friend Pockets waits with the Clown Car. Bring him the costume piece and the door pops open: hop in and he drives you to the next stop.

Energy and naps

Teddy starts with 100 energy (the F2 screen calls it Hitpoints) and three naps (Lives). Pests and flying things wear him down; a bone gives 25 back, and Teddy's green wobble ball is worth a whole extra nap. When his energy runs out Teddy is tuckered out and naps; he wakes at the start of the stop he was on. When all the naps are used up, the game is over.

Press F5 to save your game and F6 to load it.

pages.head: Moving and Hopping
pages.html:
Moving and Hopping

Left Right
or A D		Walk. Teddy turns to face the way he is walking.
Up or WHop! Tap it for a little hop, hold it to hop higher. Let go of Up and Teddy goes back to walking, so to hop onto something, hold the arrow key toward it, press Up, and let go of Up when you are high enough.
Q EHop up and to the left (Q) or right (E) in one go. Holding Up and Right together won't do it - use Q and E, and hold them as long as you would hold Up.

How high can a corgi hop?

Two blocks easily. Three blocks if you hold Up the whole way and steer at just the right moment: Teddy scrambles up anything he can get his front paws over. Four blocks, never. Walls that tall need another way around, and there always is one.

Ledges

Awnings, branches, clotheslines, bridges and tightropes can be hopped up through from below and stood on from above.

Things that lift

Fountain jets, subway steam vents, trampolines and the Clown Club's stage lift push Teddy up into the air. Walk into one, ride it up, and steer off the top.

pages.head: Teddy's Tricks
pages.html:
Teddy's Tricks

Teddy knows a ton of tricks, and every one of them is good for something. The five he learns on the way are on the number keys along the top of the keyboard, in the order he learns them.

SpaceSpeak. WOOF! The bark rolls ahead the way Teddy faces (after a hop, it goes up). Squirrels, cats, pigeons and geese clear right out. Barking is the only thing a cat napping in a doorway respects.
DownDig. Digs up the block under Teddy's feet: bones sticking out of the lawn pop right out, and soft dirt or sawdust (look for paw prints) gives way to a tunnel underneath.
FFetch. Picks up Doc Leo's costume pieces when they are lying around. Press F while standing on one.
1High five. Teddy stands up and slaps whatever is just above his head and a little in front: a kid's hand held out, a bunch of balloons.
2Sit pretty. Sends up a heart that floats straight up two blocks. Anybody with a SIT? bubble over their head is won over.
3Spin. Twirls a little whirlwind out to each side. Revolving doors start turning (go through quick, before they stop), and people asking for a SPIN love it.
4Play dead. Hold it and Teddy flops flat as a rug. Flying discs, bowling pins and custard pies sail right over him.
5Roll over. Shakes loose a tumbleweed of corgi fluff that rolls ahead and knocks over stacks of things.

pages.head: Things to Find
pages.html:
Things to Find

Treats

Dog biscuits are everywhere, 10 points each. The F2 screen counts them as Money. Kids and clowns hand out more for a good trick.

Bones

A bone gives Teddy 25 energy and 50 points. Most of them are buried; look for one end sticking out of the ground and dig.

Balloon dogs

Doc Leo's balloon animals floated loose from the suitcase. Three bob somewhere up high in every stop: 250 points and 10 energy each. They are never on the way; they are worth the detour.

Teddy's wobble ball

His favorite toy: green, lumpy, and it giggles when it rolls. Gwinn has it in the backyard and won't sit for anybody, but a good WOOF makes her drop it. Grab it while it wobbles: an extra nap and 500 points.

The Dog House

A tiny red library on a post in front of the blue house on Maple Street, all dog books. Hop up on the painted-rock cubby underneath: fetch (F) a book to carry along (250 points), and nose open the paw-knob drawer for dog snacks.

Root beer

Doc Leo always orders root beer. There is a stand on the Clown Club midway: fetch him a frosty mug (500 points).

Doc Leo's costume

One piece per stop. Some are lying around and must be fetched (F); some are caught on balloons, or held by a kid who wants to see a trick first. F2 shows everything Teddy is carrying.

Backyardthe felt fedora
Maple Streetthe green tie
The parkthe red sneakers
Downtownthe rubber chicken
The Clown Clubthe red nose

Clown Club tickets

At the Clown Club's big top, the turnstile takes three tickets. Doc Leo's friends give them out for tricks: Honker wants a high five, Bubbles wants a sit, and Twirly wants a spin.

pages.head: Who's Who
pages.html:
Who's Who

Friends

  • Doc Leo: the friendliest hobo clown in the Clown Club, and Teddy's person.
  • Pockets: drives Doc Leo's little red CitiCar between stops today, with Teddy beside him in the front seat, his head out of the window. Has a pocket for everything except costume pieces.
  • Honker, Bubbles and Twirly: Clown Club members working the midway.
  • Presto: the Clown Club's magician, warming up the crowd on the downtown plaza. Doves flutter out of his hat. They are harmless; just magic.
  • The parade: the Clown Club's drummer, banner and balloon clowns, marching down Main Street toward the Big Show.
  • Juggles: a busker downtown. He means well. His bowling pins go everywhere.
  • The kids: on porches and benches all over town. Do a trick and they share.

Pests and nuisances

  • Squirrels nip (8 energy). Bark first.
  • Cats nap in doorways and will not budge. Bark.
  • Geese guard the covered bridge in the park. Bark, from a respectful distance.
  • Pigeons peck (10 energy). Bark.
  • Flying discs, pins and pies fly at head height: discs cost 8 energy, Juggles' pins 12 and the Clown Club's custard pies 15. Play dead or hop.
  • The Pie-O-Matic test-fires custard pies backstage for the finale, one every couple of seconds, straight down the tunnel. Nobody is at the controls. Duck, and slip past it just after it fires.
  • Sprinklers on Maple Street blast Teddy back where he came from. Wait for them to rest.

Gwinn

She is everywhere Teddy goes, and she leaves a mess behind her. If she bumps into Teddy she gobbles one of his treats and bolts. She was adopted and is still learning her manners: SIT means nothing to her yet, but she does listen to a bark. She is not bad. She is just Gwinn.

pages.head: The Stops
pages.html:
The Stops

1. Doc Leo's Backyard

The tutorial yard: hop the garden boxes, walk the clothesline, bark at the squirrel, dig up bones, and climb the old oak (hop straight up through its branches) for the fedora. Gwinn is doing zoomies with Teddy's wobble ball: bark and she drops it. The back fence is too tall; dig under it.

2. Maple Street

The green tie is caught on yard-sale balloons under a porch roof: high five them. A cat is napping in the hedge arch, and the sprinklers come and go. Stop at the Dog House library for a book and a snack.

3. Puddlewick Park

Ride the fountain over the hedge, sit pretty for the kids on the bench (one of them has Doc Leo's red sneakers), and bark the geese off the covered bridge. Fall in the duck pond and Teddy paddles; the far bank is too high to climb out, so take the bridge.

pages.head: More Stops
pages.html:
More Stops

4. Downtown

The rubber chicken landed on a fire escape, leash and all: the subway steam vent will blow Teddy up there. Biggles Department Store is in the way and too tall to climb: spin the revolving door, go through (Gwinn is in the shoe department), and spin your way out. Under the construction shed, Juggles' pins come flying: play dead until they pass, and slip past Juggles just after a throw. Out on the plaza, Presto pulls doves out of his hat, and the Clown Club parade marches down Main Street all the way to the Bijou, where the CitiCar waits.

5. The Clown Club

Three tickets get you through the turnstile (and the root beer stand is right there on the midway). Roll a fluff ball into the bowling pins under the bleachers, play dead under the Pie-O-Matic's barrage of practice pies, one pie at a time, spin through the stage door, then dig through the sawdust and ride the stage lift up. Gwinn has the red nose, in the spotlight. She won't give it up... unless somebody shows her how to sit nicely. Then the nose goes to Doc Leo, the show goes on, and afterward the whole Clown Club parades out into the night with Teddy riding on the CitiCar roof.

pages.head: Credits and Registering
pages.html:

Starring Teddy as himself, with Gwinn as herself (sorry) and Doc Leo, the friendliest hobo clown in any clown club, and his red 1976 CitiCar.

items.title: Teddy Hint Book
items.note: Answers hidden: use the red film
items.intro: Stuck? Find your question, then slide the red film over the answer. Try one answer at a time; Teddy believes in you!

hints.q: I found the costume piece. How do I get to the next stop?
hints.a: Bring it to Pockets at Doc Leo's little red CitiCar at the end of the stop. The door pops open: hop in and he drives you on.

hints.q: What are the floating balloon dogs for?
hints.a: They're Doc Leo's balloon animals: three in every stop, up high and never on the way. 250 points and 10 energy each, so take the detour.

hints.q: Where is Doc Leo's fedora?
hints.a: Up in the top branches of the old oak. Hop up through the branches one at a time, then stand on the fedora and press F.

hints.q: Gwinn is running laps with a green ball!
hints.a: That's Teddy's wobble ball. She won't sit, but she does listen to a bark: face her and press Space as she zooms by. Grab the ball while it wobbles for an extra nap.

hints.q: The squirrel keeps nipping me.
hints.a: Bark first! Press Space while facing it and it scampers off.

hints.q: The back fence is way too tall.
hints.a: Look for the soft dirt with paw prints at its foot. Stand on it and press Down to dig a tunnel under the fence.

hints.q: How do I find the buried bones?
hints.a: Look for a bone end sticking out of the lawn, stand on it and dig. Each bone gives back 25 energy.

hints.q: A cat is napping in the hedge arch and won't move.
hints.a: Cats only respect a bark. Face the cat and press Space.

hints.q: The sprinkler keeps blasting me back.
hints.a: It only sprays for a while. Wait until it rests, then trot right across.

hints.q: How do I get the green tie?
hints.a: It's caught on yard-sale balloons by the white house's porch. Stand under them and press 1 to high five; the tie drops down.

hints.q: What is the little red box on a post?
hints.a: The Dog House, a tiny library. Hop onto the rock cubby under it, press F for a book, and stand by the paw-knob drawer for snacks.

hints.q: The kids on the porches hold out a hand.
hints.a: That's a high five waiting to happen! Press 1 under the hand and they toss you a treat.

hints.q: How do I get over the tall hedge?
hints.a: Walk into the fountain's jet. It lifts Teddy up; steer off the top and over the hedge.

hints.q: Which kid has Doc Leo's red sneakers?
hints.a: One of the kids on the bench. Stand near the SIT? bubble and press 2 to sit pretty, and the heart wins them over. The sneakers drop right down.

hints.q: The geese won't let me on the covered bridge.
hints.a: Geese only respect a bark. Face them and press Space from a few steps away, and they waddle off the bridge.

hints.q: I fell in the duck pond!
hints.a: Teddy paddles. Swim back to the near bank, climb out on the rock by the bridge stairs, and try the bridge again.

hints.q: The rubber chicken is up on a fire escape.
hints.a: Stand on the subway steam vent and it blows Teddy up. Steer onto the fire escape and fetch the chicken (leash and all) with F.

hints.q: Biggles Department Store is in the way.
hints.a: Press 3 to spin at the revolving door, then hurry through before it stops. Spin again to get out the other side.

hints.q: Bowling pins keep bonking me under the shed.
hints.a: That's Juggles practicing. Hold 4 to play dead until the pins fly over, then scoot ahead. Pass Juggles himself right after he throws: each new pin starts just in front of him.

hints.q: The turnstile won't let me in.
hints.a: It takes three tickets. Honker wants a high five (1), Bubbles wants a sit (2) and Twirly wants a spin (3).

hints.q: Bowling pins block the tunnel under the bleachers.
hints.a: Press 5 to roll over. The fluff ball rolls ahead and knocks the stack down.

hints.q: The pies keep coming!
hints.a: The Pie-O-Matic fires one every couple of seconds. Hold 4 to play dead as each one comes, then scoot ahead. Pass the machine right after it fires: each new pie starts just in front of it.

hints.q: How do I get up on the stage?
hints.a: Spin through the stage door, dig through the sawdust, crawl along to the stage lift and ride it up.

hints.q: Gwinn won't give back the red nose!
hints.a: Show her how it's done: sit pretty (2) near her. She sits too and drops the nose at her feet. Grab it and bring it to Doc Leo.

hints.q: Some say the felt-maker left something behind on Maple Street.
hints.a: Some say a lot of things. But a raised paw reaches places a hop can't. Fetch Doc Leo's bow tie first.

hints.q: Where do I raise my paw?
hints.a: At the Dog House, the tiny little library on the lawn in front of the blue house. Once you've carried the bow tie past it, the right end of its rock cubby holds you up.

hints.q: Paws and all, step by step?
hints.a: After fetching the bow tie, hop up onto the right end of the Dog House's rock cubby and give a high five (1) to the knot in the hedge just right of the red door. Inside, hop up to the shelf and fetch the felt egg (F). Leave by the red door.

items.title: Clown Club card
items.name: TEDDY
items.back: The bearer saved the Big Show and is welcome at every Clown Club show, free of charge, forever. Honk twice at the turnstile. No pies in the face (unless asked).

news.head: A corgi joins the Sandbox family
news.html: Teddy the corgi is back, and this time he's left the sandbox for the big town! Teddy's Little Big Adventure sends him from Doc Leo's backyard to the Clown Club's Big Show with nine tricks on nine keys. Our testers' favorite trick? Play dead. Our testers' favorite dog? Don't ask Gwinn.

news.head: Ask the Sandbox: why so many dogs?
news.html: Readers keep asking why our games star so many dogs. Simple: the office has two of them, and they won't stop walking across the keyboard. If you find a typo in one of our manuals, now you know who to blame. Send your own pet's best trick to the BBS and we may print it in the next Scoop!

news.head: Since last issue: The crown is back
news.html: Sandcastle Knight was our first game made for the PC speaker alone, and you played it everywhere. You found the secret dial-up in about a week, and the GIF in its file area, the SysOp and his corgi, is the most downloaded picture on the board. The most-asked question: how do I get past Gwinn? Toss her a tennis ball. She can't resist.

news.head: Around the Sandbox: The little red car has a name
news.html: Doc Leo's little red CitiCar is in this game (his friend Pockets drives it between stops, with Teddy in the front seat), and you keep asking what it's called. Read the license plate: THE CHEZ. It's a 1976½ CitiCar, 100% electric, and it charges at about a mile an hour, so it's plugged in out front more often than not. Sharp-eyed players saw one before: Grandpa's CitiCar in In The Year 2000!

news.head: In the workshop: A mystery for Halloween
news.html: Our first mystery is nearly done, and it's coming in October for a good reason. Final Curtain puts you in a trench coat at the Paragon Theatre on Halloween night, 1936. Every clue is in the game, and the solution comes in three parts: who, how and why. Our testers have argued about it over lunch for a week.

news.head: Letters: "Is Gwinn a bad dog?"
news.html:
"Gwinn flattened every castle and fell asleep on the crown. Is she a bad dog?" - Two readers, one of them a little sister

The Scoop replies: No. Gwinn is a good girl who knocks things over. In this game she might even learn a trick. Keep an eye on her.
